core_obligations: Reduce through epsilon (proof lines 21520-21527): since epsilon_{Y,*} is the identity on underlying presheaves it reflects isomorphisms, and the description of the pullback gives epsilon_{Y,*} a_Y^{-1} = pi_Y^{-1} and the same for X, so it suffices to show that the displayed four-term composite is an isomorphism.

Identify the composite (proof lines 21528-21543): the composite begins with pi_Y^{-1}f_small,*F = epsilon_{Y,*}a_Y^{-1}f_small,*F and ends at f_big,etale,*pi_X^{-1}F, so it is exactly the statement of part (1) of the comparison lemma for proper morphisms, which gives the result.
proof_roadmap: Use that epsilon_{Y,*} reflects isomorphisms, together with the description of the pullbacks, to reduce to an etale statement.
Recognise the resulting composite as part (1) of the proper comparison lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the fppf version of the proper push-pull identity, deduced from the etale case (statement lines 21513-21517). The proof (proof lines 21519-21543) reduces by the reflection of isomorphisms through epsilon_{Y,*} and the description of the pullbacks, then identifies the four-term composite with part (1) of the proper comparison lemma. H2: one reduction and one identification.
